about.title: About System Design Lab
about.body: A practice bench for system design: build a design, run it on a simulator in your browser, and see what holds and what breaks. Everything runs on your machine.

shell.desktopNotice: This lab is built for screens at least 1280 pixels wide. It still works here, but some panels will be cramped.

leaderboard.placeholder: Rankings of the cheapest passing designs will appear here once accounts exist.

engine.failed: The simulator could not start. Check your connection, then try again.

db.no-replica: {node}: the primary failed and there is no replica to take over.
db.primary-down: {node}: the primary failed; {replicas, plural, one {# replica} other {# replicas}} left.
db.promoted: {node}: a replica was promoted to primary.

fault.no-target: A fault found no matching component and was skipped.
fault.unsupported: This fault is not simulated yet, so it was skipped.

node.overloaded: {node} is overloaded and has started rejecting requests.

calibration.invalid: World parameter “{field}” has an invalid value.

client.no-path: {node} has no path to a server.

edge.unknown-node: A connection points to a component that no longer exists.

graph.cycle: The design loops back through {node}; requests would go round forever.
graph.no-client: Add a Users component so something sends requests.

limits.too-many-instances: The total number of instances is over the challenge limit.
limits.too-many-nodes: There are more components than the challenge allows.

node.unknown-kind: {node} is a component type the simulator does not know.
node.unreachable: {node} gets no requests: nothing connects to it.

componentDescription.client: Where requests come from: the people using your system.
componentDescription.lb: Spreads incoming requests across the servers behind it so no single one is swamped.
componentDescription.web-server: Runs your application code and answers HTTP requests. Add CPUs or copies to serve more.
componentDescription.postgres: A relational database that keeps data safe. Read replicas share the reading load.

calibration.webServiceMs: Web: time to serve a request (ms)
calibration.webQueuePerGb: Web: waiting requests per GB of memory
calibration.webCostPerVcpu: Web: monthly cost of the first vCPU ($)
calibration.webCostPerExtraVcpu: Web: monthly cost per extra vCPU ($)
calibration.lbQueueSeconds: Load balancer: seconds of traffic it can hold
calibration.lbCostPerReplica: Load balancer: monthly cost per node ($)
calibration.lbMaxUtilizationForLatency: Load balancer: busy level where delays start
calibration.pgQueueSeconds: PostgreSQL: seconds of queries it can hold
calibration.pgFailoverMs: PostgreSQL: time to promote a replica (ms)
calibration.pgMaxUtilizationForLatency: PostgreSQL: busy level where delays start
